The net interest margin (NIM) is a measure of the difference between the interest income generated by banks or other financial institutions and the amount of interest paid out to their lenders, relative to the average balance of assets and liabilities. It is expressed as a percentage and is calculated as follows:

\[ \text{Net Interest Margin} = \left( \frac{\text{Interest Income} - \text{Interest Expense}}{\text{Average Balance of Assets and Liabilities}} \right) \times 100 \]

This ratio helps in assessing the profitability of a bank's asset-liability management and its ability to generate returns on its assets while managing its liabilities effectively. A higher NIM indicates better profitability for the institution.

\[ \text{Average monthly downloads} = \frac{29.3}{12} \]
